impact: Cloud infrastructure destroyed on 2 Nov; second DDoS on 15 Nov slowed recovery
date_note: Second attack reported 15 Nov; the first attack was on 2 Nov. Time of day not stated.
title: Russian host Beget hit by second large DDoS while rebuilding cloud destroyed on 2 November
summary: Hosting provider Beget said on 15 November it faced a second large DDoS attack in two weeks, aimed, it said, at disrupting recovery; The Moscow Times gives 2.1 Tbit/s, iStories up to 850 Gbit/s. On 2 November it said its cloud infrastructure had been destroyed; Beget blames unnamed hackers. Topvizor Journal, relayed by directline.pro on 17 November, said 95% of shared-hosting and 94% of dedicated servers were running again.

evidence.quote: уже восстановлена работа 95% серверов виртуального хостинга и 94% выделенных серверов
Мощность сегодняшней атаки составляет до 850 Гбит/с.

plain: A big Russian web host was hit by a second flood attack while still rebuilding from an earlier one that wiped its cloud service.
exec: Shows how one provider's outage and data loss can take down many customers' sites and email at once.
action: General advice: Beget customers: check your own off-host backups and follow the provider's status channel. Others: confirm you can restore hosted sites and DNS elsewhere.

validation.note: The Moscow Times and iStories, two independent outlets, agree on dates and Beget's statement; attack size differs between them; Beget's own Telegram was not read. Headquarters city not stated in sources, so pinned at country level. Follow-up 23 Nov: Topvizor Journal (republished by directline.pro, 17 Nov) gives the restored server shares and over 150,000 sites back from backups; www1.ru (15 Nov, citing Beget's Telegram) gave over 215,000 sites; the site counts were not reconciled, so neither is in the summary. Removed an occurred_at of 12:00 that no source states.

review.note: figure evidence added for up to 850 Gbit/s (iStories) and 2.1 Tbit/s (Moscow Times); 95 and 94 percent and dates match
